findings.claim: Ruling (c) removes `base` from `pin` only, but node `cut` still prints `base` 'from $pin.output' and its output_format requires it. Contracts row H17 says the same, as do `gauntlet-design.md:14`, `worktree-cut-design.md:7` and `:230`, so applying the ruling as written leaves the cut hand-off with no source for a required field.
findings.failure_scenario: The edit drops `base` from pin's output_format (`:118`, `:82`) and leaves `cut` (`:130-132`) unchanged. Under Archon's strict field access (`workflow-language.md:617`), `$pin.output.base` is an undeclared field, so `archon validate workflows` fails at load. If the builder keeps the field, H17's 'base from $pin.output' has no producer. G-32/D-33 is the precedent the ruling cites: it dropped `uncommitted` from pin and from cut together (H16, H17). This ruling does not name cut, H17 or the gauntlet phase-4 hand-off, and cut's `base` has no reader either (finding 2.41: land, fail and kill never read it).

findings.claim: The ruling names only `pin` and leaves the landing half of G-83 (finding 2.67) unruled. Node `repin` still declares `base` required (`:253`), and `land/scripts/pin.py` still prints 'base the full hash of that tip' (`:343-344`). Both rest on `.shared/pin.py`'s `pin() -> { branch, base }` (`worktree-cut-design.md:63`), which the ruling's removal of the merge-base branch leaves with no value for a present branch.
findings.failure_scenario: Read narrowly, `.shared/pin.py` keeps returning `base` but loses the present-branch rule, so a resumed round whose `<round>__retree` branch already exists has an undefined `base`. That breaks repin's required field, and `land/tests/test_pin.py` (`:349`) has nothing to pin. Read broadly, `.shared/pin.py` drops `base`, and repin's output_format and stdout contract (rows S14, S15) silently lose their producer. Either way, a field nothing reads (`retree`'s `with:` at `:259` takes only `branch`) is still built and tested in landing. That is the CLAUDE.md 1.3 waste the ruling meant to remove, left standing in one of the group's two cited files.
